races.name: Follow @AtTheRaces On Instagram Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Circuit Breaker
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse trained by Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill, returning after 64 days off; best recent effort was a third over 16f on Standard, but has an inconsistent profile (form -26364) and will need closers to get a genuine race.|
runners_data.comment: Circuit Breaker shaped with promise when third three starts back, and his overall profile — experience over today's trip and going, plus a rating of 82 — makes him an appealing each-way proposition, though he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Benvoy
runners_data.note: Won over 2m at Lingfield on soft and is clearly bred for this trip, but is a true hold-up horse awkwardly squeezed into midfield here given the volume of closers; 124 days between runs is a significant query and Jo Davis has had no runners in the past 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after a 124-day absence, Benvoy has at least shown he handles today's going, and a third two starts back offers mild encouragement; the 154 lb burden is a stiff ask, however, for a gelding rated 68.

runners_data.name: Roland Garros
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in this field and holds the critical pace-making role over 2m; runs just 6 days after his last start, wears tongue tie and a hood, and his controlled lead should be uncontested — his best recent effort is a third on Standard over 16f, though this step to 2m stretches him.|
runners_data.comment: Roland Garros was fourth last time and third two starts back, showing respectable recent form in this contest, and he has experience of today's distance and going; the main risk is that last week's run comes just six days ago.

runners_data.name: Wise Counsellor
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type from Gary & Josh Moore, who have been in strong form (4/19 T14); returns after 56 days and has been running exclusively on Good going, with only 3 runs from 13 on similar Standard — the AW surface is a mild query.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third on two separate occasions in recent starts, Wise Counsellor holds solid claims here on going he has encountered before, and our rating of 75 marks him out as a live danger — the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts, and a 56-day absence adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: Diamond Bay
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old who wears a hood and is a genuine closer by inclination, though the redistribution here means he is unlikely to get the ideal rear position he needs; won twice over 2m+ on Good and is in some form (2nd last time), but the Standard AW surface has not been his friend (6/15 sim-going).|
runners_data.comment: Diamond Bay shapes as a leading threat here — rated 82 by our assessors and ranked top of eight — with experience over today's trip and going, and a second last time out hinting he's returning to form after 26 days off; the risk is he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Flamingo Rose
runners_data.note: Has been off the track for 401 days — a serious fitness concern regardless of talent; wears a tongue tie and is a natural hold-up horse who won once over 2m on Good, but the long absence and being mapped into midfield rather than her natural position make this a difficult ride for the 7lb claimer.|
runners_data.comment: Flamingo Rose won two starts back but has been off the track for over 400 days, and her rating ranks her seventh of eight runners, making her very hard to fancy; she does have experience of today's trip and going, which is a small crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Further Measure
runners_data.note: The most course-and-distance accomplished runner in the field with 14 starts on similar going (3W4P, sim-going 14/15) and a recent winner at 2m on Standard; tracks up prominently, wears a hood, and Mrs Charlotte Owen (7lb claim) is a real asset — profile suits the expected race shape strongly.|
runners_data.comment: Further Measure won five starts back but has finished fourth or worse in his four subsequent outings, making consistency the obvious concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 70 gives him a edge over his official mark of 60, though 146 lb is no light burden.

runners_data.name: Beaune
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old who is lightly weighted and wears a hood; three wins in six runs on similar going (3W6P) suggest she handles the surface well, but is a true hold-up type repositioned into midfield, and stepping up from 12-14f to 2m for the first time is a significant unknown for a young horse.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Beaune faces a stiff ask, and a sequence of thirds and worse in his last five starts does little to inspire confidence; the one crumb of comfort is he has run over today's going before and returns on a fresh enough 14-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Roland Garros is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 2m amateur handicap on the Lingfield AW, and with no genuine rival for the lead, he should be able to bowl along at a controlled, unhurried pace entirely on his own terms — a significant tactical advantage over 2 miles. Further Measure is the only other runner with genuine prominent leanings and will likely track Roland Garros into second or third early, creating a small, compact lead group with the remainder strung behind. The bulk of the field — Circuit Breaker, Wise Counsellor, Benvoy, Diamond Bay, Flamingo Rose, and Beaune — are all natural hold-up types, though several of them (Benvoy, Diamond Bay, Flamingo Rose, Beaune) have been redistributed into the midfield on the map because there are far more closers here than can realistically all settle at the rear, meaning their actual race positions will be more compressed than ideal and their finish-line kick may be blunted. This race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or close to a controlled pace, as the steady tempo set by one uncontested leader creates a genuine advantage for those tracking him rather than waiting in a pack of closers who may all need the same ground late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Garros Dictates, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Roland Garros leads uncontested at a comfortable gallop and Further Measure tracks him closely throughout.
scenarios.body: Roland Garros controls every fraction, the pace is too steady to string out the field, and those sitting handy get first run into the straight; Further Measure's strong course and distance form (sim-going 14/15, 3W4P) makes him the likeliest to pounce at the right moment.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and the compressed midfield generates enough sustained momentum for hold-up types to get competitive.
scenarios.body: A genuinely honest gallop over 2m can bring the closers into play in the final quarter-mile, particularly for runners who settle well and quicken late; Circuit Breaker and Wise Counsellor are the truest hold-up types in the field and have the best chance of finishing through if this unfolds.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Roland Garros dictates a very slow tempo, the field comes to him late but he has conserved enough to repel all challengers.
scenarios.body: On a flat AW track with no pressure, a horse leading at a crawl can produce a devastating turn of foot from the front; Roland Garros has shown he can stay the trip and has tongue tie helping his breathing, making a front-running victory plausible if rivals leave it too late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If the field becomes strung out early despite intentions, allowing Benvoy, Diamond Bay or Flamingo Rose to find their natural rhythm and finish best of all.
scenarios.body: This depends on those redistributed hold-up runners genuinely getting space to settle and produce their finishing effort, which is a lower-probability outcome given they are racing out of their ideal position in a compressed pack; Benvoy's sole course win at 2m on soft and Flamingo Rose's one win in this trip on good both give slim hope if pace and position conspire in their favour.

watchPoints.text: Further Measure's dominance of the sim-going data (3W4P from 14 on Standard) makes him the most empirically grounded runner in the field — watch whether Mrs Charlotte Owen positions him close enough to Roland Garros to secure first run.|

Flamingo Rose has not raced in 401 days and is being ridden by a 7lb claimer; if she is ring-rusty or fails to settle in her unnatural midfield position, she could get outpaced on the turn for home and cause interference in a compressed pack.|

Roland Garros ran just 6 days ago and while he is fit, watch whether his early stride is as sharp as usual — if he misses the break or is slow into stride, the entire pace dynamic collapses with no other front-runner to fill the role.|

The volume of redistributed hold-up types (Benvoy, Diamond Bay, Flamingo Rose, Beaune) bunched in midfield creates a risk of traffic problems in the straight — riders on Circuit Breaker and Wise Counsellor should be watched to see if they can find clear daylight early enough.|

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Musical Force
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner with Harry Eustace handling her at peak fitness (28 days fresh); her best form came on Standard AW going at 7f and she steps back to 6f here — David Probert's positive style suits if she can lead cleanly, but may find Romotoso's presence costly in a duel.

runners_data.name: Mystic Unicorn
runners_data.note: Flagged as a hold-up type who fades in the finish; her only start produced a modest ninth over 7f on this surface, and there is little in the profile to inspire confidence over a shorter, faster 6f with two pace horses likely to impose a stern gallop.

runners_data.name: Nightspell
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with an unknown profile, having finished fourth on her sole start over 6f at Goodwood — Jack Mitchell takes the ride for Ross Burdon, but the uncertain running style and limited data make her a genuine unknown quantity best treated with caution.

runners_data.name: Past Passion
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's filly has placed twice at 5f on Good ground and is now stepping up in trip to 6f on AW Standard — her prominent style is well-suited to tracking this contested pace, and the extra furlong may unlock more stamina for Tyler Heard to exploit late.

runners_data.name: Pertinent
runners_data.note: A modest performer who has twice finished ninth over 7f and once tenth over 5f — the hold-up style and flagged tendency to fade in the finish combine poorly with a contested pace scenario on a surface she has limited experience over.

runners_data.name: Polly The Sniper
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's filly ran a promising fifth on her only start over this exact 6f trip at Goodwood, and her prominent style maps well to tracking the front-runners into the straight — William Cox is in profit for the yard over 14 days and brings tactical nous.

runners_data.name: Romotoso
runners_data.note: William Knight's filly finished third on her debut over 6f at Goodwood and is the most experienced pure front-runner in the field — Taylor Fisher partners her, and if she can see off Musical Force for the lead, her class and trip experience make her the most dangerous leader.

runners_data.name: Enriched
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's yard is in red-hot form (T14: 5/17) and Cieren Fallon's presence on an unraced debutante signals strong stable confidence — going preference and running style are both unknown, so the wildcard element is genuine and she should not be dismissed.

runners_data.name: It'sbeenemotional
runners_data.note: Laura Mongan's filly has course-and-distance form on this Standard AW surface (fourth and seventh at Lingfield 6f) and her prominent style suits the race shape — 54 days between runs is worth monitoring, but Georgia Dobie's familiarity with the horse may help settle any freshness.

runners_data.name: Last Dandelion
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' filly has the widest experience in the field and has won at 6f Standard AW, making her the most likely closer to benefit if the front-runners burn each other out — Marco Ghiani's strength in running makes her a logical each-way contender at a price.

races.paceDynamic: Romotoso and Musical Force are confirmed front-runners who will dispute the lead from the off over this 6f Lingfield AW contest, creating a genuinely contested early pace rather than a soft, uncontested gallop. With both fillies likely to push for position, the race should be run at an honest clip from the gun, compressing the advantage available to either leader by the time the field straightens. Prominent runners Polly The Sniper, Past Passion, and It'sbeenemotional will look to track the speed and remain competitive without burning too much petrol in the duel ahead of them. The contested pace scenario tilts this race shape in favour of prominent-to-midfield types who can track a genuine gallop and arrive with a late kick — hold-up runners who need significant pace collapse will find conditions marginally less favourable given the likely honest tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Romotoso and Musical Force fight for the front and set an honest pace, softening each other up by the turn.
scenarios.body: The duel up front burns both leaders' reserves, handing the initiative to prominent trackers who can hit the rising Lingfield straight with energy in the tank. Past Passion and Polly The Sniper, sitting just behind the pace with tactical awareness, are ideally placed to sweep through and nail the tiring leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates Clearly
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners establishes a clear lead early and the other capitulates or is restrained.
scenarios.body: With a solo leader controlling tempo, the pace becomes honest but not brutal, giving that horse the best chance to control the fractions and hold on. Romotoso, with a solid third on her only start over this exact 6f trip, is the more likely candidate to secure the role and boss the race from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough and sustained to string the field out, leaving genuine closers with ground to make up the straight.
scenarios.body: Last Dandelion has course-and-distance form on this surface and can close from off the pace if the gallop is truly end-to-end. Enriched, the debutante from Tom Clover's in-form yard, represents the wildcard — lightly raced and unknown, but Cieren Fallon aboard suggests connections expect a forward showing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leaders Survive
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner truly commits to a strong gallop and the field dawdles through the early stages.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race over 6f at Lingfield could compress the finish and reward whoever gets a clear run up the rail, potentially flattering the leaders who find themselves in front with petrol to spare. Mystic Unicorn and Nightspell, both needing something to go wrong ahead of them given their hold-up profiles, would need this slow-burn scenario to deliver — but the presence of two confirmed front-runners makes this the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Romotoso and Musical Force are both confirmed front-runners — watch whether either capitulates for the lead in the first furlong, as the outcome of that early duel will define the shape of the entire race.

Enriched is an unraced debutante from a yard firing at 5/17 over 14 days with Cieren Fallon booked — a strong market move before the off would signal she is well-prepared and could outclass the field on debut.

Past Passion steps up from 5f to 6f on AW Standard for the first time — if the extra furlong suits her prominent style, she is capable of finishing considerably closer than her 14-length win-less record on Good ground might suggest.

Last Dandelion's course-and-distance form (3rd at Lingfield 6f Standard) gives her a genuine edge over rivals with no AW experience — watch whether Marco Ghiani is able to position closer to the pace than her hold-up profile might suggest given the competitive early tempo.

Mystic Unicorn and Pertinent both carry flags for fading in the finish — if either is prominent early and weakens through the final two furlongs, it could create traffic problems for hold-up horses attempting to thread through a tiring pack.

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Fighting Poet
runners_data.note: An 8yo hold-up specialist whose recent form (406892) includes very limited sim-going form (0 wins, 1 place from 15 efforts on Standard), and the true hold-up role he wants will be occupied by others in a congested rear division — his chance is materially discounted in a front-run shape.
runners_data.comment: Fighting Poet showed up well with a second last time out, but that ninth two starts back clouds the picture, and he remains winless in his last six; the 135 lb burden is no help, though he does have experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Pride Eye
runners_data.note: Carries a finish-fade flag and has primarily run at 8-10f on Goodwood; the step up to 1m4f on AW for the first time looks a tough ask, and trainer Mark Rimell's T14 strike rate of 0/5 does not inspire confidence at this meeting.
runners_data.comment: Pride Eye returns on going she has experience of and after a 21-day break looks fit enough to go, but consecutive fourths in her last two starts and a win only five starts back suggest she needs more to get competitive from a mark of 50.

runners_data.name: Snooker McCrew
runners_data.note: Won over 1m on Standard AW (1/8f/STA) and placed there, but has never run beyond 10f, making the step to 1m4f a genuine stamina uncertainty; the 7lb claim of Alfie Redman is a minor positive if the trip proves within range.
runners_data.comment: Snooker McCrew won four starts back but has since posted three consecutive fifth-or-worse finishes, and 135 lb is no featherweight. He has experience of today's going and returns after a 28-day break, though his recent consistency gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Someone's Wish
runners_data.note: A 6yo who has run extensively at 16-17f on Goodwood and Heathrow-style tracks, so shortening to 1m4f may not be in his favour; 71 days off the track and a trainer T14 of 0/6 suggest limited immediate readiness, and sim-going form (0 wins, 3 places from 15) is modest.
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of the field on our ratings, Someone's Wish posted back-to-back thirds four and five starts back and has experience of today's trip and going, making him a clear threat despite being winless in recent starts; the main concern is a 71-day absence.

runners_data.name: Summer Evening
runners_data.note: Has run 12 times on Standard going without a win and only two places; a 4yo hold-up type who finished 8th in her last two AW starts, she is mapped out of her deepest position in a race shape that is least likely to suit her — a hard profile to endorse here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with three consecutive eighths and ninths making her very hard to fancy, Summer Evening at least returns on a quick turnaround having run over today's distance and going before, but our figures rank her eighth of ten.

runners_data.name: Churchill's Spirit
runners_data.note: A 3yo hold-up type stepping up in trip; his three-run STA history shows a 3rd and a 6th at 8-10f but this is uncharted territory at 1m4f, and he's racing out of his natural back-of-field position, which further blunts his appeal in a race likely to be dictated from the front.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Churchill's Spirit faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a third two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement, but 126 lb makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Star Suepreme
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this field; trainer Lemos De Souza has landed 3 of his last 9 runners and this 3yo is taking a step up to 1m4f for the first time, raising a slight stamina query, but on Standard AW the ability to control fractions compensates — this is her race to lose.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Star Suepreme faces a stiff ask here, though she has experience of today's going and returns on a reasonable 22-day break.

runners_data.name: Foinix
runners_data.note: Blinkered hold-up type whose last six runs include a win and a second at 1m2f on Standard AW, showing the surface and trip are squarely in his favour; though the congested hold-up division means he may not get to settle as deep as ideal, his recent upward trajectory (877321) makes him the most dangerous of the back-markers.
runners_data.comment: Foinix arrives in fine fettle off a seven-day turnaround, his recent form reading an encouraging sequence of first, second and third in his last three starts, and he has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 140 lb is the one query, but his current momentum makes him our pick.

runners_data.name: Charles Morin
runners_data.note: Has blinkers applied and a hold-up profile, but his last AW run (11th of 12 at 1m2f, Standard) is a concern, and stepping back from 16-19f handicaps to 1m4f is a significant change in setup — carry rated only for the scenario where the pace truly heats up late.
runners_data.comment: Charles Morin showed real promise when second and third in recent starts, and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims at 135 lb; the risk is his two latest unplaced efforts suggest he needs to bounce back sharply.

runners_data.name: Douglas Dc
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has placed at 1m2f on AW and Standard ground multiple times; Tony Carroll's yard is in excellent recent form (5/48 T14) and Ghiani is an AW specialist — the horse most likely to physically sit closest to the pace and challenge in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time, Douglas Dc has run over today's trip and going and comes back fit on a 14-day turnaround carrying 135 lb, with our rating of 52 ranking him fourth of the ten; the risk is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

races.paceDynamic: Star Suepreme is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of ten, and on Standard Lingfield AW over 1m4f she is highly likely to dictate from the front without a genuine challenger disputing the lead — Douglas Dc (prominent) is the only horse likely to press forward and sit close enough to apply any pressure, but even he is not a natural pace-setter and will probably settle just off the lead rather than hassle Star Suepreme directly. The result is a single-file, controlled gallop through the early stages with Star Suepreme controlling every fraction, a setup that historically on this flat AW surface rewards the horse who can dictate and then stretch the field in the straight. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Charles Morin, Foinix, Fighting Poet, Summer Evening, and Churchill's Spirit are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield slots, meaning the true back of the field will be more congested than the map shows, and only Pride Eye, Snooker McCrew, and Someone's Wish are most likely to genuinely settle deepest. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours the front-runner Star Suepreme and any prominent tracker who can latch onto her slipstream (Douglas Dc), while the hold-up brigade faces a pacemaker-controlled tempo that may never truly set them alight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Star Suepreme Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Star Suepreme jumps cleanly, establishes the lead by the first furlong, and controls a steady-to-moderate pace without Douglas Dc closing up to apply pressure.
scenarios.body: Star Suepreme sets every fraction she chooses, the field strings out behind her, and with no rival forcing her wide or increasing the tempo she conserves enough energy to kick clear in the straight; this scenario is a pure front-runner's paradise on a flat track where energy conservation from the front is maximised.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Douglas Dc tracks Star Suepreme closely throughout and outstays her in the final two furlongs as the leader's lack of experience at this trip tells.
scenarios.body: Douglas Dc, the one genuine prominent horse in the field, sits a length or two off the pace and strikes as Star Suepreme ties up; at 1m4f a front-runner making all on this surface is vulnerable to a well-positioned tracker who has been conserving on the bridle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough — perhaps because Douglas Dc does push Star Suepreme — to set up a fast final two furlongs that rewards a late run from the hold-up pack.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop compresses the field and burns out the front two, creating a window for a hold-up horse coming from off the pace to pick up ground in the straight; Foinix, whose recent form shows a 1-2-3 sequence and who handles this surface, is best positioned to benefit despite being mapped out of his natural position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Finish, Closers Fail
scenarios.trigger: If Star Suepreme sets a falsely slow pace that concertinas the field, with hold-up types never getting a clear run late and the race degenerating into a scrappy sprint finish.
scenarios.body: The compressed field causes traffic problems for horses attempting to come from off the pace, and the winner is the horse closest to the fractions throughout rather than the most talented finisher; hold-up horses tagged as redistributed are particularly vulnerable here as they cannot truly dominate from the position they occupy.

watchPoints.text: Star Suepreme — if she misses the break or is headed early, the entire race dynamic collapses, as she is the only confirmed pace-setter in a 10-runner field.

Douglas Dc — watch whether Marco Ghiani elects to press Star Suepreme or sits patient; if Ghiani pushes forward and applies pressure, the pace becomes genuinely contested and hold-up chances improve materially.

Foinix — with blinkers and five hold-up types competing for the same ground at the rear, watch the early running order closely; if he fails to find a clear passage in the straight he cannot demonstrate his recent improvement.
Pride Eye — carries a stamina/fade flag and steps up sharply in trip on AW for the first time; if she starts travelling strongly at halfway it is a significant form reversal signal worth noting.

Someone's Wish — 71 days off the track and stepping down substantially in trip from habitual 16-17f targets; if he moves freely early it suggests the layoff has not dulled his condition and he could outrun his modest profile.

races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Perfect Ruler
runners_data.note: A hold-up type returning from 92 days off for Marco Botti, whose 14-day strike rate is solid at 4/19; no form on Standard AW going in the recent hist and a tendency to finish mid-pack leaves questions about whether she can produce a decisive late run in a race likely to be run at a modest pace.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Perfect Ruler nevertheless rates above her official mark and shapes as a genuine threat here, having run over today's trip and carrying a workable 135 lb from stall seven; the chief concern is 92 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Grey Sands
runners_data.note: Genuine flat-mile form on Standard AW — one win and a placed run at this trip in similar conditions — and wearing a tongue-piece, but Kim Bailey & Mat Nicholls have no runners in the 14-day window; her natural racing style sits at the back and she will need a strong pace that looks unlikely to materialise here.
runners_data.comment: Grey Sands showed his best when third three starts back and a winner four starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims at a rating of 62; the main concern is a 57-day absence and back-to-back disappointing efforts since.

runners_data.name: Ten Cuidado
runners_data.note: Persistent finisher in the data but carries a fade flag and has a 0W0P record in five runs on Standard ground; Mark Usher sends her here with one winner in 12 runners over 14 days, and though she sits in midfield on the map she is a true hold-up operator who needs the race to be run genuinely to deliver any late surge.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with his recent form reading unplaced-unplaced-seventh-fourth-unplaced, Ten Cuidado ranks last on our figures here and looks hard to fancy, though he does have experience over today's trip and going, and returns after 41 days off.

runners_data.name: Henfield
runners_data.note: The lone pace-setter here, winning most recently over this exact course-and-distance combination and showing a placed effort at the same track; the fade flag is a concern in the final furlong if rivals close, but an uncontested lead on Standard ground at this trip is a significant advantage and David Probert is an excellent judge of front-running tactics.

runners_data.name: Ernie McCrew
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning — four fifth-place finishes and a 0W0P record across seven runs at a mile on Standard going — and ridden by 5lb claimer Millie Wonnacott; a genuine rear-of-field runner placed into midfield on the map, she is the shortest-priced horse in the field in terms of exposed form suggesting a ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Ernie McCrew has shown steady midfield form, and with experience over today's trip and going, plus a lively 12-point gap between his official mark and our rating of 61, there is a strong case he is handicapped to strike — though his winless run in recent starts remains the key concern.

runners_data.name: My Old Mate
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on Good ground over a mile at similar grade give him the strongest recent form in the field; carries top weight at 140lbs and last ran just eight days ago, and while Jude Fernandes (7lb claimer) reduces that burden, his single run on Standard going produced a ninth — a genuine concern given the surface today.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins make My Old Mate the one to beat here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and returning just eight days on from his latest success suggests connections are keen to press home his advantage, with his rating of 72 underscoring his superiority at the top of this field.

runners_data.name: Venturing
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll sends her in with a 5/48 strike rate over 14 days and she has shown placed form at this trip on Standard AW, though two consecutive fourths and no wins in eight career starts define her profile; a hold-up runner by history who will need the race to open up in the straight, which the pace map suggests is unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Venturing has at least shown some mid-race consistency with a pair of fourths in recent outings, and he has run over today's trip and going before; 135 lb from stall two is the challenge, and he remains a tough nut to crack at a rating of 60.

races.paceDynamic: Henfield is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no rival likely to challenge for the lead aggressively, he should bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on Lingfield's flat Polytrack mile. That uncontested pace sets up a race in which the lead is never truly pressured, making it difficult for hold-up horses to generate the sustained tempo-change they need to reel the leader in. Several runners — My Old Mate, Grey Sands, Ten Cuidado, and Ernie McCrew — are genuine hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield simply because there are too many rear-ward horses for the map to accommodate them all; in reality, most will race closer to last and will need a significant injection of pace to close. The shape firmly favours horses who can sit just off Henfield's shoulder in the prominent-to-midfield bracket and pick him up in the final two furlongs, rather than those coming from deep who rely on a truly run race to deliver their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Henfield Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Henfield dictates a modest, uncontested gallop and his rivals leave him alone through the first six furlongs.
scenarios.body: Henfield sets a comfortable tempo from his low draw, conserving energy through the middle portion before kicking again inside the final furlong; horses sitting closest behind him — ideally those with prominent or early-prominent profiles — get the best possible tow into the straight. With no genuine pace pressure the race becomes a test of stamina and tactical awareness, suiting those who travel smoothly rather than those who need the race run fast.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Henfield's gallop is just fast enough to string the field out and one genuine hold-up runner produces a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: A fast enough pace on Standard ground leaves Henfield vulnerable in the final furlong and a horse who has settled well off the pace — most likely My Old Mate, whose recent wins at this trip stand out — collects with a sustained run from two furlongs out. The obstacle is that most true hold-up types here are racing out of their natural position and must sustain their challenge much earlier than ideal, making this scenario harder to deliver.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If a second runner challenges Henfield for the lead early, lifting the gallop and turning this into a genuine test of stamina.
scenarios.body: Should My Old Mate or another prominent-moving type decide to go with Henfield sooner than expected, the pace quickens and the race becomes more truly run, leaving the leader vulnerable but also stretching the hold-up horses who have to cover more ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail, Front Wins Easily
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses are simply too far back and the pace is too sedate for any late run to materialise in the straight.
scenarios.body: Henfield pings clear in the straight completely unchallenged, having enjoyed a perfect solo lead throughout, while the genuine closers find themselves finishing into empty places having never been able to build momentum from the rear. This extreme version of Scenario A is limited only by Henfield's own modest OR of 51 and the fade flag attached to him.

watchPoints.text: Henfield's ability to secure an unchallenged lead is the single most important factor — watch the first furlong closely to confirm no other runner presses him, as an uncontested gallop dramatically boosts his chance of lasting home.

My Old Mate carries top weight of 140lbs and has only one run on Standard AW ground (finished ninth) — if the surface proves slower-feeling than his Good-ground wins, his ability to produce the same late burst is in serious doubt.

Grey Sands and Ten Cuidado are both genuine hold-up horses placed artificially into midfield on the map; if they are forced to sit last as expected, watch whether the pace in the straight is sufficient for either to close meaningfully over a mile.

Henfield is flagged as a fader — if his gallop softens markedly from the two-furlong pole, the horse travelling most smoothly in second or third at that point becomes the primary beneficiary regardless of nominal running style.

Three of the seven runners are partnered by apprentice or conditional jockeys (Alfie Redman 7lb, Finley Marsh, Millie Wonnacott 5lb, Jude Fernandes 7lb) — tactical errors in a slowly-run race could compress or extend margins unpredictably in the straight.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Classified Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Miraflores
runners_data.note: Poor recent form (876499) with zero wins or places on similar going in five attempts; a natural hold-up horse whose style-fit suffers here as the field pushes natural backmarkers into midfield, and Taylor Fisher faces a tactical puzzle at OR=43.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a pair of ninth-place finishes in her most recent outings, Miraflores is hard to fancy here despite having experience of today's trip and going; ranked last on our figures, she faces a stiff task from stall four carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Raqraaq
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with 1W4P on similar going across 15 runs, but recent form is patchy (5th, 8th, 12th) and the step back to 7f from 8f trips is worth noting; natural hold-up style means he will be further back than ideal in this compressed field, with David Probert needing a clear run late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a third four starts back his best recent effort, Raqraaq returns after 36 days off carrying 135 lb from stall six, and while he has run over today's trip and going before, his latest two outings suggest a difficult task here.

runners_data.name: Turpin
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter by redistribution from a hold-up profile — visored for the first time, which connections often deploy when seeking a different response; his sim-going record is weak (4/12, no wins or places) and he must sustain an unfamiliar frontrunning role over 7f.
runners_data.comment: Turpin shaped with some promise when third last time out, but has been winless in his last six starts and that run of mid-pack finishes — including a ninth three starts back — suggests he finds winning difficult; the experience over today's trip and going at least offers some encouragement from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Victory Sound
runners_data.note: Form shows consistent placing (3rd, 3rd in recent starts) and six placed efforts from 15 on similar going; hold-up type with enough tactical speed to sit closer than usual given the sparse pace, making him a natural fit for the tracking role in Scenario A.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in his last four starts, including third two runs back, Victory Sound brings solid recent form to this contest and has run over today's trip and going before; the main risk is that he remains yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Zaltalla
runners_data.note: Lightly raced on AW with 12 runs on similar going yielding 1W4P, and last run just 5 days ago raises a freshness query for Tom Queally; however, three consecutive placings (3-2-3) suggest excellent current form and he is versatile enough to sit mid-division and quicken.
runners_data.comment: Zaltalla has been knocking at the door, finishing third, third, and second in three of his last four starts, and he returns just five days on from that latest effort with fitness on his side, having run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Dora Vita
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly at OR=45 whose five career runs are all on Good going bar one 6th at Lingfield AW — the Standard surface is largely unexplored territory and that unknown is a significant concern; natural hold-up type bumped into midfield by field congestion, with Jonny Peate needing to find room.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Dora Vita faces a stiff ask here; a third two starts back offers some crumb of comfort, and she has run over today's trip and going before, but 130 lb from stall nine makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Mademoiselle Belle
runners_data.note: Her entire career form of 1W6P has been built on Good going at shorter trips (5-6f), making this 7f Standard AW assignment a double-ask on trip and surface; natural hold-up horse mapped into midfield, and sim-going figures (10/15) reflect that AW exposure has not translated to results.
runners_data.comment: Rated highest in the field, Mademoiselle Belle has run over today's trip and going and is fresh after 28 days off, with a second in recent starts showing ability — yet her last two efforts were disappointing, and that form dip is the key question she must answer.

runners_data.name: She's Crafty
runners_data.note: Showed a smart 2nd on Good over 7f at Goodwood and 5th on similar going, suggesting she handles the trip; 49-day absence is a minor concern but George Margarson is adept at placing horses fresh, and Jack Mitchell can hold her up before delivering a trademark late challenge.
runners_data.comment: She's Crafty shaped well for second three starts back and our rating of 59 ranks her second of twelve here, making her a genuine threat despite being winless in recent starts; the chief concern is a 49-day absence returning from that layoff.

runners_data.name: Coiled
runners_data.note: Flagged as a finisher who fades late — a damaging tag in any race — and his record on similar going is almost non-existent (2/15) while form reads 0007 in recent starts; natural hold-up horse pushed into midfield by congestion and the style-fit concern compounds his already poor form profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with no placed efforts among them, Coiled is hard to fancy on these figures, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a reasonably fresh 13-day break.

runners_data.name: Edergole's Gift
runners_data.note: Holds equipment (tongue-tie, breast-girth) and ran 4th at 6f on Standard AW 10 days ago, showing some recent currency; Cieren Fallon is a high-quality booking and the drop back to prominent territory is tempting, but his natural hold-up style means he may be further back than ideal in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Hold The Press
runners_data.note: 187-day absence is the dominant factor — Marco Ghiani rides for a trainer with just 1 run in the 14-day window, and the horse's AW record (1W4P from 15 runs) was largely built before this lengthy break; natural hold-up type whose lack of race fitness makes a forward position unlikely despite redistribution into midfield.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 187 days, Hold The Press faces a stiff ask from stall 11 carrying 135 lb, and a ranking of tenth of twelve on our figures hardly inspires confidence; experience over today's trip and going is about all he brings.

runners_data.name: Maury
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard AW 42 days ago (1/7f/STA) which is the most directly relevant recent piece of form in this field; Georgia Dobie takes the ride and the horse's natural hold-up style, while redistributed to midfield, means Maury needs a clear run late — the winning form over course and distance keeps him squarely in view.
runners_data.comment: Maury showed he can win in recent starts, landing a victory five runs back, but a fourth followed by eighth, ninth and seventh since then give pause; he has run over today's trip and going, and the 135 lb burden is no help to a horse rated just 46 officially.

races.paceDynamic: Turpin is the sole identifiable pace-setter here, redistributed from a natural hold-up role to the front because no confirmed front runner exists in the field — he will set a controlled, unhurried gallop on Standard Lingfield AW over 7f, unlikely to be strongly pressed for the lead. With just one horse doing the donkey work at a sustainable tempo, the pace figures to be honest rather than searching, creating a race that sets up best for horses able to track the pace in the prominent-to-midfield berths and quicken off a steady gallop in the straight. The field is saturated with genuine hold-up types — Raqraaq, Maury, Edergole's Gift, Hold The Press, Miraflores, Coiled and Dora Vita are all natural backmarkers who will be mapping further forward than their instincts want — and only the most tractable of those will secure a useful position. The tactical verdict is clear: horses with the ability to sit just off Turpin's shoulder in the first three or four, rather than those committed to finishing runs from the rear, are best placed in this pace shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Lead, Tracking Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Turpin sets an uncontested, controlled pace and those able to sit second or third on the rail quicken past him in the straight.
scenarios.body: Turpin's lone-lead at a measured gallop compresses the field and removes any premium on finishing pace, meaning horses settled just behind him avoid traffic and hit the line fresh; this shape heavily rewards Victory Sound and Zaltalla, both of whom have the tactical versatility to sit close to the pace and have placed form on this surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Thread Late
scenarios.trigger: If Turpin's tempo is genuinely slow enough to create a bunch finish where late closers find gaps in a compressed straight.
scenarios.body: A slow early pace paradoxically creates chaos in the home straight as twelve runners converge simultaneously, and any hold-up horse that avoids traffic at the 2f pole can deliver a strong late run; Zaltalla and She's Crafty, both capable of finishing powerfully on Standard going, are most likely to thread through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Turpin, finding himself completely uncontested and relaxed, dictates at a pace that demoralises the field and kicks clear turning for home.
scenarios.body: An unchallenged Turpin could simply convert his natural hold-up stamina into a staying effort by conserving energy from the front — his connections have placed him to exploit this scenario and the visored headgear suggests they need something different; the risk is his redistribution from true hold-up means this is an unfamiliar role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stragglers Pile In
scenarios.trigger: If several redistributed horses attempt to push forward simultaneously, creating a messy early scramble and a fast early pace that collapses late.
scenarios.body: A chaotic pace scenario would see the field string out and favour the freshest-legged hold-up types arriving late, but most of the genuine backmarkers in this race have poor recent form figures and sim-going records that do not inspire confidence; Raqraaq, with 1W4P on similar going, and Maury, a recent course winner on Standard, are the most credible beneficiaries.

watchPoints.text: Maury is the only runner with a recent win over course, distance and going (1/7f/STA 42 days ago) — watch whether Georgia Dobie can manoeuvre from a congested midfield to replicate that effort in the straight.

Zaltalla arrives on consecutive placed finishes (3-2-3) and just 5 days' rest — monitor whether the quick turnaround dulls his finishing effort, as Tom Queally's positioning in the first half-mile will be critical to his chance.

Turpin carries the whole burden of pace as a horse redistributed from a hold-up role — if he backs off the gallop or is reeled in before the 2f pole, the race shape collapses and the front end becomes chaotic for all prominent trackers.

Hold The Press returns from 187 days off for a trainer with minimal recent runners — a well-beaten return is the likely script, but any unexpected freshness burst from stall position could disrupt the anticipated race shape in the early stages.

The field contains at least seven natural hold-up horses all competing for midfield real estate — watch the opening two furlongs for bumping or traffic issues that could compromise multiple runners simultaneously before the race settles.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Classified Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Megaphone
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up specialist who has been out-of-the-placings consistently on this surface (sim-going record 0W1P from 15 runs), making this Standard AW trip a tough ask despite a young claimer aboard; likely to be deepest of all late runners.
runners_data.comment: Megaphone has run over today's trip and going, and his speed rating of 59 gives him an edge over his official mark of 50, though he arrives just one day after his last outing and is yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: No News
runners_data.note: Recent runner-up form at 6f on this surface gives a form reference, but true running style is hold-up and the field is too crowded at the rear for a clean run — likely to race closer than ideal without quite getting natural rhythm.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, No News does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and his second two starts back shows a competitive streak worth noting; however, that official rating of 46 and a tendency to fade — eighth last time out — make progress hard to predict.

runners_data.name: Regal Guest
runners_data.note: Jack Mitchell takes the ride for Margarson, whose 14-day record (0/5) is uninspiring; Regal Guest's true home is off the pace but will be squeezed toward midfield in this shape — recent AW going record is modest (0W1P from 9 runs).
runners_data.comment: Regal Guest has been winless in his last five starts, finishing no better than sixth in recent outings, and our rating ranks him tenth of eleven here, making him hard to fancy at face value; he does at least return on a quick turnaround with distance and going experience to his name.

runners_data.name: Rovinia
runners_data.note: Roger Teal runner who has finished second on four of her last five starts including at 7f-8f on Good, showing consistent placed form; a natural hold-up type who will need things to happen in front of her, but her finishing consistency is the strongest in the field.
runners_data.comment: Rovinia has been a model of consistency, finishing second in three successive starts, and returning here after just 13 days suggests she is in fine fettle; yet to score in recent starts, the risk is whether she can finally convert her place form into something more.

runners_data.name: Vitalline
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has won twice at 6f on Standard AW and carries a tongue-tie; sits deepest of all stylistically but the sim-going record (2W4P from 15) is the best strike rate here — a genuine threat if the pace is fast enough to set her alight.
runners_data.comment: Vitalline won three starts back and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour, and our rating of 55 gives him a live chance from stall three; the concern is consecutive ninths in his last two outings.

runners_data.name: Crown The Future
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's 3yo is the lone confirmed front-runner and the only horse in this race with a genuine pace role; Carroll has been active (5/48 in 14 days) and Myla Coppins rides for the first time here — STYLE_FIT flag notes she may be racing slightly out of her optimal mode in terms of tactics, but she is still the dominant pace influence.
runners_data.comment: Crown The Future has run over today's trip and going before and, ranked top of the field on our rating, makes a compelling case as the chief threat here; the risk is that he has been winless in his last five starts, with only a third to show in that sequence.

runners_data.name: Power Cut
runners_data.note: Chelsea Banham's 3yo has run entirely on Standard AW over shorter trips (5f-6f), making this 7f step up a question; hold-up style is out of position in this field and the 42-day absence adds further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Power Cut at least has experience of today's trip and going to draw on, and his rating edges above the official mark — but a 42-day absence and a consistent pattern of mid-to-rear finishes leave him with plenty to prove from stall two carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Ruiz
runners_data.note: Simon Dow's 3yo carries a hood and has a concerning recent record — flagged as fading in finishes, with no wins or places from seven Standard AW runs; true hold-up style is rendered even less effective in this shape and the step up from 10f to 7f is inconsistent form.
runners_data.comment: Ruiz has been winless in his last five starts, with a string of mid-division and unplaced efforts offering little encouragement, and our figures rank him last of eleven here. The experience over today's trip and going is some consolation, but he faces a stiff task from 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Chloe's Courage
runners_data.note: John Ryan's 4yo wears a hood and has placed four times in five recent starts including at 7f on Good, making her the most in-form of the closers; a natural hold-up type who will be pushed toward midfield in this shape but her recent placed form makes her a noteworthy runner.
runners_data.comment: Chloe's Courage arrives here just 11 days after her latest run, showing a third three starts back yet winless in recent starts, and while she has run over today's trip and going, carrying 135 lb from stall 10 leaves her with plenty to find against this field.

runners_data.name: Dupont Circle
runners_data.note: Georgia Dobie's ride returns from 57 days off — the longest absence in the field — with a hood, a sparse AW record (0W0P from 4 runs), and a true hold-up style that is unlikely to get a clean position; the freshness angle is the only positive angle to take.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Dupont Circle faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and returns after 57 days off, but a career-high 135 lb from stall 11 does little to ease the case for him.

runners_data.name: Horus
runners_data.note: Michael Attwater's 4yo wears a hood and a tongue-tie and has been running over 6f on Standard AW recently; the step to 7f alongside a redistribution onto midfield from his natural hold-up position makes this a difficult profile, though the trainer has had 1 winner from 13 in 14 days suggesting minor stable form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Horus has at least run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 52 offers a small edge over his official mark of 44; however, consistent finishes in the rear half of the field make it hard to fancy him turning things around from stall four.

races.paceDynamic: Crown The Future is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 7f AW contest at Lingfield and, with no genuine rival likely to press her hard from the gates, she should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop through the first half of the race. The remainder of the field is composed almost entirely of hold-up types — Megaphone, No News, Regal Guest, Rovinia, Vitalline, Chloe's Courage, Dupont Circle, Power Cut, Ruiz, and Horus — the vast majority of whom have been redistributed on the pace map because there are simply too many closers for the rear to accommodate them all; in reality, several including Chloe's Courage, Dupont Circle, and Regal Guest are most likely to push closer than their natural style and will sit in a dense mid-pack group. With Crown The Future able to control tempo without being pressured, she sets an honest but not punishing fractions-scenario — a steady-to-moderate early gallop that does not guarantee the closer-heavy field will get a strong enough pace to close off. This race shape most clearly favours a horse that can race prominently or pick up from just off the leader in the straight, as the controlled pace is unlikely to set up a fast-finishing sprint for true hold-up runners who need a truly run race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crown The Future Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Crown The Future dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the hold-up pack fails to reel her in down the straight.
scenarios.body: Crown The Future sets a sustainable pace from flag to flag, and with no rival willing or able to press her, the tempo stays honest-but-not-searching, making it very hard for closers to close the gap in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Crown The Future's controlled gallop is just fast enough to string the field out but a strong finisher tracks into a gap from mid-pack.
scenarios.body: A moderate tempo compresses the mid-pack but one of the redistributed hold-up types who secures a better-than-expected tracking position picks up sharply once daylight appears in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Finisher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Crown The Future sets an overly modest gallop and a genuine hold-up runner produces a strong sustained late run from the rear.
scenarios.body: The slow early pace ironically opens the race up for any runner who can produce a powerful finish over the final furlong, bypassing a strung-out and tiring mid-pack.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Challenger Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed mid-pack runner who secures a prominent early position produces a front-running or prominent-style win against the pace map.
scenarios.body: A horse such as Regal Guest or Dupont Circle, forced closer to the pace than typical, finds itself in an unexpectedly advantageous position and sustains that effort to the line.

watchPoints.text: Crown The Future — if she gets an uncontested lead through the first two furlongs, watch whether Myla Coppins (5lb claimer) allows the gallop to drop to a crawl, which would dramatically improve her winning chance and devastate late runners.

Rovinia — consistent placed runner who has finished second four times recently; watch whether Marco Ghiani can get her into a tracking position rather than being trapped in the hold-up pack, as her style fit here is better than her redistribution implies.

Vitalline — the best sim-going strike rate in the field but needs a strong pace; if Crown The Future goes slowly, Josephine Gordon will need to make an early decision about whether to commit and close — watch her position at the 3f mark.

Chloe's Courage — hood-wearing 4yo with four places from five starts is the form standout among the closers; watch whether Darragh Keenan can secure a closer position than her natural style, which the pace map suggests she may be forced into anyway.

Dupont Circle — returning from 57 days off is the biggest freshness flag in the race; watch her early movement in the paddock and whether she travels smoothly into the race, as a hold-up type this fresh on a Standard AW surface is an unknown quantity.

races.name: Download The At The Races App Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Peregrine Falcon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent form on standard going reads 3-3-5-3-2 at 5f — consistent placegetter but yet to win in 15 starts on similar surfaces; stepping up to 6f here may help stamina but a solo leader sets a tough target from the rear for Ryan Kavanagh (3lb claim).
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back and runner-up five starts back, Peregrine Falcon arrives fit on 18 days' rest with experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 64 suggests she holds solid claims — the risk is she has been winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Big Bard
runners_data.note: Proven C&D winner (1/6f/STA) for Gary & Moore who are in strong recent form (4 from 19 in 14 days); in reality a true hold-up type placed mid-division here because the field is loaded with closers, so his preferred last-to-first style is compromised — headgear noted (hood/p), returns after 69 days off which is a stamina question.
runners_data.comment: Big Bard has a win among his last five outings but has since posted a ninth and a sixth, and 69 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 133 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Balon d'Or
runners_data.note: Simon Dow's 5-year-old carries a hood and has shown zero wins or places from 15 similar-going runs at this trip range, a deeply concerning stat; his natural closer's style is squeezed into midfield by the volume of hold-up horses in this field, further reducing his already limited route to victory.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Balon d'Or nonetheless catches the eye as the second-ranked runner on our ratings, with experience over today's trip and going and a lively 14-day turnaround suggesting he arrives fresh; the concern is that his recent form has yet to translate into a placing.

runners_data.name: Alashos
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over C&D (1/6f/STA) and has trainer Chris Gordon firing (2 from 3 in 14 days); 57-day absence needs treating with some caution but the course win and natural prominent style make him ideally placed to track Dashing Donkey and strike turning in.
runners_data.comment: Alashos won three starts back but has posted a fourth and seventh since, and 57 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 132 lb from stall seven, and a rating of 60 gives him a slim edge over his official mark.

runners_data.name: Due Date
runners_data.note: Charlie Wallis's gelding wears a visor and is a true closer by trade, here mapped to midfield because genuine hold-up horses outnumber rear positions — his best form (2/6f/GOO, multiple STA wins) suggests ability when getting a true run, but 45 days off and a compressed field position limit his scope.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a sixth, two sevenths, and an unplaced run among recent efforts, Due Date is hard to fancy ranked ninth of ten on our figures, though that second last time out and experience over today's distance and going offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Dashing Donkey
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter; form figures of 0-5-0-4-9 show limited finishing effort but his role is to lead, not finish — William Stone has no runners in the 14-day window and the drop to 6f (from 7-8f recent runs) is a positive flag for an outright front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Dashing Donkey faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and comes in reasonably fresh at 19 days since his last outing.

runners_data.name: Porfin
runners_data.note: Phil McEntee's 8-year-old runs just 5 days after his last start and has a rock-solid record on standard going (13 from 15 outings on similar surface), placing or finishing fourth consistently; a prominent style and solid consistency make him a dependable shape-fitter even if a win is elusive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Porfin is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns just five days after his latest fifth.

runners_data.name: Diamond Dreamer
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who wears blinkers and has 12 runs on standard going (0W4P) — David Probert rides but the horse's best efforts tend to come when pace is genuine, which it won't be here with only one front-runner; 47-day break adds mild uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Diamond Dreamer has run over today's trip and going before, but he arrives winless in his last six starts, with only a third and a second offering any encouragement; 47 days off and 135 lb from stall 10 add further questions for this midfield prospect.

runners_data.name: Express Train
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type for Richard Phillips; his standard-going record (0W2P from 7 runs) is modest and recent form shows a rare third from 6 starts — Jonny Peate takes the ride but at 14 days since last run and OR 60, he needs luck from the rear that this race shape is unlikely to supply.
runners_data.comment: Express Train has run over today's trip and going, carries a workable 135 lb from stall three, and our rating of 64 edges him clear of his official mark — but he is winless in his last five starts, and that persistent shortfall in form is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Happier
runners_data.note: In-form prominent racer who has won back-to-back (1/5f/GOO, 1/5f/STA) but both wins came at 5f, not 6f — the step in trip is the key question here; Toby Moore's 7lb claim reduces the weight and trainer Martin Keighley is live (1 from 2 in 14 days), making him dangerous if he handles the extra furlong.
runners_data.comment: Happier arrives in cracking form, winning on each of her last two starts, and she has experience of today's distance and going to call upon. Carrying 135 lb from stall five, our rating has her top of these, and she looks the one to beat.

races.paceDynamic: Dashing Donkey is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 6f AW handicap at Lingfield and, with no natural rival to force the tempo, Jack Mitchell can dictate a controlled, uncontested lead at a pace entirely of his choosing. Behind him, Alashos, Porfin, and Happier will push forward to claim prominent positions, creating a compact, organised early order rather than a contested sprint for the lead. The hold-up brigade — Diamond Dreamer, Express Train, Peregrine Falcon, and the redistributed Big Bard, Balon d'Or, and Due Date — will be operating from further back than ideal on a track where a solo leader setting a moderate gallop can prove very hard to reel in over 6f. This shape strongly favours front-to-prominent runners who can track the pace on a short rein and pounce early in the straight; true closers face a stern test when no genuine pressure softens up the leader. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear cleanly — Big Bard, Balon d'Or, and Due Date are genuine closers redistributed into a midfield mapping, and of those three, Due Date (visor, course experience) and Big Bard (proven winner here) are likeliest to actually find a decent position mid-division, but none will get their true preferred ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dashing Donkey Leads Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Dashing Donkey is allowed a soft lead and the pace stays controlled throughout the 6f.
scenarios.body: Mitchell settles Dashing Donkey in a rhythm unchallenged, the gallop is moderate enough to preserve his stamina, and the hold-up horses simply have too much ground to make up in the final 2f on this track. Prominent horses Alashos and Happier are best placed to chase him home but lack the firepower to close a controlled leader down.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If Alashos or Happier press Dashing Donkey from the off and force the pace fractionally higher, weakening him in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A marginally quicker early tempo drains Dashing Donkey's reserves and leaves him exposed inside the final furlong, allowing a prominent tracker to sweep past. Alashos has a Lingfield win on the board and Happier arrives on the back of back-to-back wins with in-form handler Martin Keighley, making either a credible beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and the redistributed hold-up types find a clear run from mid-division.
scenarios.body: Big Bard is a proven winner over C&D in standard going and, if he can travel smoothly in midfield — his redistributed position — he retains a finishing threat over the final 2f. Diamond Dreamer and Express Train are genuine hold-ups who need the pace to collapse and a gap to appear, both of which are less certain given the solo, self-regulating leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Chaotically
scenarios.trigger: If a contested, fast pace develops due to Porfin or Happier aggressively disputing Dashing Donkey's lead and the whole field races beyond their comfort zone.
scenarios.body: A ragged, hot gallop scrambles the race shape and opens the door for the genuine hold-up horses operating from the back — Peregrine Falcon and Due Date both show course-relevant standard-going form and could pick up pieces late. This scenario is the least likely given the moderate pace expected, but Due Date's visor and front-foot history means he could push harder than anticipated if freshened up after 45 days off.

watchPoints.text: Dashing Donkey sets the race pace in isolation — watch whether Jack Mitchell elects to bowl along or dawdle, as the tempo he sets in the first 2f will define whether hold-up horses have any chance of landing a blow.

Happier steps up from 5f to 6f off a back-to-back winning streak — if the extra furlong suits, his prominent style and Keighley's yard form make him a major pace-shape beneficiary, but failure to stay could see him drop away sharply inside the final furlong.

Big Bard returns after 69 days off for a yard in good recent form (4/19 in 14 days); fitness is the unknown after over two months away and, combined with his cramped midfield position relative to his true running style, he is a horse to watch for signs of rustiness early.

Alashos is 57 days fresh and carries a hood (p), but the C&D win on standard going is directly applicable — watch to see if Charles Bishop sits just off Dashing Donkey and whether the horse travels with his usual early fluency after the absence.

The trio of redistributed closers (Big Bard, Balon d'Or, Due Date) will all be hunting the same mid-division ground — crowding and traffic trouble around the home turn is a genuine risk if they converge on the same space with limited racing room on the Lingfield AW straight.
